properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 12:03PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall to the area. The first ongoing
front is expected to bring 1 to 2 inches of rain to the Juneau area
the rest of today, with the second round of heavy rain bringing an
additional 1 to 2 inches through tonight. More localized higher
amounts are possible due to terrain effects, but overall the
moderate to heavy rainfall is expected to last into the overnight
hours and Friday morning with not much of a break between the rounds
of precipitation.

The precipitation amounts that have fallen today and the additional
forecasted amounts expected through Friday morning are expected to
bring rises to small creeks and rivers in the area. While small
creeks and rivers may reach bankfull, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.


For Jordan Creek near Juneau:
At 11:00am the stage was 7.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.7 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.9 feet is expected around 1:00pm Friday.
Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around 10:00am Friday.
Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around 10:00pm Friday.

Impacts:
At 9.2 feet: This is the stage when Jordan Creek is at bankfull and
water will begin to inundate areas along the edges of the creek near
Race Reality and Jordan Square.
At 9.7 feet: Water will inundate the Jordan Square's front and back
parking lots, around Jordan Creek office condominiums with up to one
foot of water. Some residential driveways will be flooded and cut
off.
...
For Montana Creek at Back Loop Bridge:
At 12:00pm the stage was 11.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 14.7 feet is expected around 7:00am Friday.
Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around 5:00am Friday.
Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around 9:00am Friday.

Impacts:
At 14.5 feet: Water begins flowing over the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road. Bankfull conditions at the gauge with water
starting to inundate adjacent undeveloped fields along Mendenhall
Loop Road.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN AND SMALL CREEK RISES THROUGH FRIDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Glacier Bay; Eastern Chichagof Island; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 12:03PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle.
The first ongoing front is expected to bring 1 to 1.5 inches of rain
to the northern half of the panhandle today. The second round of
heavy rain is expected to bring an additional 0.5 to 1.5 inches
tonight into Friday morning, with the higher end QPF amounts
expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands. More localized lower or
higher amounts are possible due to terrain effects. A brief lull in
the heavier precipitation amounts is expected during the afternoon
hours today.

Even higher rain amounts are possible for parts of the central
panhandle associated with the front tonight as its low develops
inland and moves northward, though there is still a lack of
confidence on the exact location of these higher rates. As of now,
the highest amounts are expected to move into southern Baranof
Island up into Stephens Passage, though some elevated rainfall
amounts may still reach Sitka and other parts of the central and
northern panhandle.

While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to
small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Friday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. However, strong northeasterly winds are forecast
this weekend and will return the river to Moderate Flood Stage, with
a steady increase through Moderate Flood Stage forecast through early
next week.

forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM EDT Thursday was 2.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early next
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near Castolon,

threatened. At 19.0 feet, the river reaches major flood stage.

Castolon, as stages at each location are practically synonymous.
